physical similarity is involved in same–different tasks, but not in numerical or physical comparison, and that only numerical representation is involved in priming tasks.

the contribution of physical stimulus similarity and numerical representation in tasks that involve number processing depends on task demands and that performance primarily relies on numerical properties in numerical comparison and priming tasks, while performance in the same-different task is primarily based on subjective physical similarity.

performance in the same-different task is best predicted by physical similarity, performance in the physical comparison task is predicted by both physical and numerical similarity, performance in numerical comparison is only predicted by numerical similarity, and performance in priming is only predicted by number.

the question of whether the contribution of subjective similarity and numerical representation is the same in different symbolic number tasks.
the question of how physical similarity and numerical representations are involved in symbolic number processing.
the fact that some of the often-used symbolic tasks used to study numerical cognition are confounded by stimulus properties.

physical similarity is not a confound in the same–difference task, but it may become a confound when the task requires explicit comparison.
physical similarity is a factor in the same–differences task and numerical representation is involved in the numerical comparison, physical comparisons, and priming task.
physical similarity or numerical representation is not the only factor that contributes to participants’ performance, but that the contribution depends on task demands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physical and numerical representations are not independent but are rather intertwined.

physical similarity and numerical similarity can both be involved in the same–differenct task, while the former is the main contributor, and that numerical representation is the only contributor in the numerical comparison task.
physical similarity and numerical representations are two different types of information that contribute to the same–different, physical comparison, numerical comparison, and primitying tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same–different and priming tasks are not suitable to study symbolic number representation.
the contribution of numerical and physical stimulus properties should be carefully considered when interpreting results from symbolic number tasks.
